The HEA, CrMnFeCoNi, was processed by vacuum induction melting under an argon atmosphere using pure metals with purities higher than 99.5 wt%.
The cast ingot was homogenized at 1273 K for 1 h and quenched in water to generate a coarse-grained structure.

To produce gradient-structured samples, tensile specimens were processed by ultrasonic surface mechanical attrition treatment (SMAT) method [33,34] at room temperature from four faces under two conditions: (i) soft processing with an ultrasonic amplitude of 40 µ m for 30 s on each face
(ii) mild processing with an ultrasonic amplitude of 60 µ m for 60 s on each face
processed by SPD via the high-pressure torsion (HPT) method [36,37] at room temperature under a pressure of 6 GPa for 10 turns

The homogenized sample contains equiaxed micrograins with an average size of ~30 µ m
some annealing twins are also visible within the microstructure as indicated by arrows in Fig. 1 a
some dark points are visible in Fig. 1 a, which correspond to micro-pores. These pores are formed during vacuum induction melting and remain in the sample after homogenization and SMAT processing.
it is evident from the low-magnification images that both samples have a deformed structure beneath the surfaces
The variations in shade of colors within grains witness some intragranular disorientations and these disorientations are more significant for the sample deformed under mild SMAT condition.

Large internal misorientation on the surface and large density of planar defects including {111} twins confirm the formation of gradient structure in the HEA after SMAT processing.
Dark-field and bright-field images indicate the formation of numerous nanograins with an average size of 25 nm after HPT processing.

The results illustrate that the coarse-grained sample has good hydrogen embrittlement resistance, but its yield strength is as low as 220 MPa.

The large elongation of 65% achieved for the homogenized sample after hydrogen charging confirms that the presence of micro-pores in the samples does not have a significant effect on hydrogen embrittlement.
The amount of hydrogen is 3.4 wt. ppm for the coarse-grained sample processed by homogenization
The HPT-processed nanograined sample exhibits a very high yield strength of 1850 MPa, but its ductility is quite low, and it breaks in the elastic region after hydrogen charging.
